Like most here have said, I don't know that the comparison to smokers or drug users is entirely fair - both of these habits are universally recognised as being harmful and detrimental both to the individual and to society as a whole. In that sense, they're not really directly analogous to obesity, since as many have already pointed out, there is a huge (cough) push towards the normalisation of obesity and its' effects, and to view chronic overweight as being a disability. The view of obesity as a disability is, IMO, completely undercut by the fact that ultimately, it is an entirely self-inflicted condition. I have certain acquaintances/extended family who are balls-deep into the HAES movement, and honestly the cognitive dissonance involved is absolutely stunning. People use conditions like hypothyroidism and PCOS - which again, I now a number of people who suffer from these, both overweight and of healthy weight - to draw attantion away from the fact that no matter how comfortable you say you are with your body, no matter how much you insist it's "genetics" or "conditions", or that you can't afford vegetables for some reason, none of our bodies defy the laws of thermodynamics, and none of them create mass out of shit you don't eat.

Anyone who has ever tried to shed a few pounds knows that it's hard - and obviously, the more you have to lose, the harder it is. Sure. I think we can all agree on that - it's hard in the sense that it involves changing a long-set habit of chronic overeating, like smoking or biting your nails. It takes willpower. But at the end of the day, like quitting smoking or biting your nails, it's not impossible. In fact, it's well within the reach of anyone with a reasonable level of self-control and discipline.

FPH is not a homogenous group, much as it may appear to be to those unfamiliar with it. I'm sure for some it's more of a simple, visceral reaction to the ubiquity of fatness in modern western societies. Speaking for myself, though, it's mainly the dishonesty/deflection/cognitive dissonance I mentioned, combined with the fact that it is basically like trying to advocate for the extreme opposite of the whole 90's "heroin chic" aesthetic. The likes of Tess Holliday - who I have a lot of issues with besides her morbid obesity - are encouraging young people to view being 300lbs+, not as a major fucking wake-up call to get healthy in order to offset the damage they are doing to their bodies, but as something to simply complacently accept as their genetic destiny, to be embraced and damn anyone who says otherwise, medical degree or no. Because doctors are all just shitlords engaged in an anti-fat conspiracy (I'm not even making it up). I've had acquaintances of 350lbs or so complain to me that their doctor was "discriminating" against them by suggesting they lose weight in order to alleviate their joint pain, for fucks' sake. No shit your joints hurt, you're carrying the equivalent of 2 to 3 extra people around with you everywhere... Jesus.

Furthermore - and this is just speaking for myself here - but jesus christ, whining about having to pay for an extra seat to accomodate your 300lb girth is just such a fucking first world problem, I really struggle to muster up sympathy. I'm sure it must be humiliating to be asked to move or change seats because you're just too fat to sit in them - but again, this is being presented as systemic oppression, rather than a wake-up call. I've worked with people in developing countries who have no idea where their next meal was going to come from, who'd lost multiple children to preventable disease because they didn't have the 50 cents for medicine. Meanwhile, we now officially have more obese people in the world now, than we have those who are malnourished. Aside from my feelings about fat people individually, the obesity epidemic is - to my mind - just another repulsive symptom of rampant global inequality, and if people are too wrapped up in their quest to #effyourbeautystandards and #honouryourcurrrves and other such tripe: honestly, I have zero fucking sympathy.
